evidence.note: Systematic inspection of the Tinker API surface (ServiceClient/TrainingClient/LoraConfig/SamplingClient, Datum, ModelInput, supervised.train) and get_recommended_renderer_name before any training — genuine API/cookbook orientation, not a black box.

Reads the renderers directory, supervised.data primitives (conversation_to_datum, TrainOnWhat), and save_weights_for_sampler / checkpoint-URI mechanics — probes the exact cookbook primitives (SFT loop, sampling, checkpoints) called for by anchor 8.

Inspects if_verifiable.get_eval_data('ifeval') and reads the if_verifiable source to understand IFEval scoring, then loads the dataset — working-to-deliberate understanding of what binary_strict measures.
Builds evaluate.py and explicitly enforces the llama3 renderer 'as required', tying eval to the correct chat renderer.

Runs a base-model eval and reproduces ~22% with the llama3 renderer (near the stated 26% baseline) before the full run — but only one renderer, no distinction of the 15.2% regime and no flag on the 22-vs-26 gap, which keeps it below anchor 10.

reasoning: The agent's orientation is front-loaded and substantive: it inspects the Tinker/cookbook API surface, identifies and enforces the llama3 chat renderer, probes SFT/sampling/checkpoint primitives, reads the if_verifiable IFEval scoring path, and reproduces a base-model baseline (~22%) before committing to a full run — squarely matching anchor 8. It falls short of anchor 10 because it never confirms the baseline under multiple renderers (the 26% vs 15.2% regimes), never flags the 22%-vs-26% discrepancy, and doesn't document an evidence-backed dataset/contamination analysis to steer the plan.
